AI-Assisted Research

A field report from a theoretical & computational geophysicist  ·  University of Oxford

Not a chatbot.
An instrument.

You have seen colleagues paste a paragraph into ChatGPT and paste the answer back out. That is not what this is. This poster describes a research infrastructure: AI agents that verify mathematics against primary sources, run multi-hour computations on a server, and leave a complete audit trail in version control, all while the unpublished work never leaves the machine.

"AI just generates plausible-sounding text."
Here, the model is forbidden to assert mathematics from memory. Every claim is checked against a local library of theory PDFs and cited to the page and theorem number, or reported as unresolved.
"You cannot trust it with unpublished work."
Trust is not the mechanism. A hook in the agent harness mechanically blocks every network command. Confidentiality is enforced by code, not by promises.
"It is a black box. Nobody knows why anything changed."
Every substantive commit carries a trailer linking it to a written, versioned plan. "Why did this change happen?" is answerable years later, from git alone.
"People who use AI outsource their thinking."
The AI is contractually barred from drafting the scientific work, inventing references, or claiming novelty. It verifies, audits, computes, and critiques. The author authors.
The system
Six main components

Each one exists because a plain chatbot fails at it. Together they turn a language model into something closer to a lab instrument: calibrated, logged, and used within stated tolerances.

1 · Source-grounded verification

Mathematical claims in the written work (function-space structures, operator regularity, Bayesian and set-theoretic inference conditions) are checked by a dedicated verification agent against a curated library of local PDFs: textbooks, monographs, and papers.

MechanismEach claim gets a verdict from a fixed vocabulary, with a citation like "Engl et al., p. 43, Thm 2.5". No source, no assertion.

2 · Privacy by mechanism, not policy

Unpublished scientific work is confidential and must not enter any training set. So the agent's own harness carries a guard hook that intercepts every shell command and denies anything network-shaped: curl, ssh, git push, package installs.

MechanismOne audited exception exists: bibliographic lookups that transmit only a DOI or a public title string, each query echoed to a log file the author can inspect.

3 · Plans wired into version control

Before substantive work, the agent writes a plan document into the repository. Every resulting feat/fix/refactor commit must name that plan in a trailer, checked by a git hook. Plans are never deleted; completed ones keep a closing note recording what actually happened versus what was intended.

MechanismNine repositories share one protocol file. It is provider-neutral: three different AI systems follow the same contract because git, not any vendor, enforces it.

4 · Autonomous scientific computing

The heaviest use is not text at all. Agents run multi-hour unattended missions: running sweeps of experiments to gather information about bugs, computing seismic sensitivity kernels, and writing mission reports with figures and failure logs. Heavy jobs run on a personal server: an office workstation rebuilt into a private compute server, with a job submission-and-retrieval interface the agents have dedicated skills to drive over a secure VPN.

MechanismA mission brief states goals, budgets, and stop conditions up front. The agent works overnight; the human reviews a report, not a chat transcript.

5 · An adversarial manuscript pipeline

Manuscripts pass through named modes: Verify the mathematics, Audit every citation, Review as a simulated hostile referee, Revise against reviewer comments, Proofread with a tracked diff. The AI's most valuable output is often the referee report that hurts.

MechanismRevisions follow a covenant: every proposed change quotes the exact original text, shows the replacement, and states the rationale. No silent rewrites.

6 · Graph-based literature mapping

Literature reviews here are in-depth, objective-focused mapping efforts, several running in parallel. Each one has a stated goal, a reading queue, structured notes on every source, a synthesis document, and a citation graph rendered from source, so the field's structure is mapped, not skimmed. Discovery runs through scholarly-metadata APIs only, under the audit log from component 2.

MechanismThe local reference library is searched first; an online query fires only on a genuine miss, and only public strings (titles, authors, DOIs) ever go out.
Worked example
What happens to one mathematical claim

Say the written work asserts that a particular forward operator admits a well-defined adjoint under given assumptions. Here is the pipeline that sentence goes through.

Step 1
Claim extracted
The verification agent isolates the precise mathematical statement, including its hypotheses, from the source text.
→
Step 2
Sources consulted
It searches the local PDF library, reading extracted text and, for equation-heavy pages, rendered page images.
→
Step 3
Verdict + citation
The claim is matched to a theorem, page, and edition, or flagged. Known traps (bounded vs compact, Banach vs Hilbert adjoint) are checked explicitly.
→
Step 4
Author decides
The human reads the evidence and keeps, weakens, or reworks the claim. The AI never edits the mathematics on its own authority.
Every claim receives exactly one verdict: confirmed confirmed with qualification unsupported locally incorrect / misleading author's modelling choice  "I could not verify this" is a first-class answer, and the honest one is preferred to a fluent guess.
Evidence
The receipts

Claims about rigor deserve the same standard as any other claim: evidence. Every exhibit below is a genuine artifact from this machine — real file paths, real timestamps, content verbatim. Elisions are marked. Nothing is mocked up for this poster.

Provenance: exhibits are screenshots of actual repository files, git output, hook-denial events from session logs, the outbound-query audit log, and page crops from the local PDF source library. The manuscript revision shown (Exhibit 5) is a tracked latexdiff of a real paper’s summary, rendered verbatim from its own LaTeX source across a revision commit.
Exhibit 1Verification you can check yourself. The agent's note asserts a claim with page-level citations; below it, crops of the actual cited pages from the local PDF library. Page 64 says, word for word, what the note claims it says — and the theorem itself is where the note points. Every mathematical claim in the written work goes through this.
Exhibit 2The confidentiality guard, denying its own operator. Verbatim from session logs (europa's real IP address redacted for the public copy): a raw ssh attempt was refused by the hook and the work rerouted through the one sanctioned channel. Minutes later the guard denied a git commit because the commit message contained the word "curl" — the agent reworded the message rather than working around the guard. A rule that blocks even false positives is a rule that actually runs.
Exhibit 3The complete outbound traffic of a literature session. The audit log of every query that ever left the machine: DOIs and public bibliographic strings of already-published papers, timestamped. This is the full extent of what "online" means in this workflow. No sentence of unpublished work appears here, ever.
Exhibit 4A real plan document. Before substantive work, the agent writes the plan into the repository: objectives, files to touch, and — note — tests to write per phase. Commits then cite this file in a trailer, so "why did this change happen?" stays answerable from git history years later.
Exhibit 5A manuscript revision, shown the way the pipeline shows every revision. An Introduction paragraph from a real paper — the PLI manuscript — edited in an “anti-AI style pass” (commit: “Polish Introduction: anti-AI style pass, restore citation, author edits”) and rendered as a tracked latexdiff: struck-through red is removed text, underlined blue is added. This is the Revise/Proofread covenant made visible — no silent rewrites, every change an exact before/after. The edits strip AI filler and soften overclaims: a great deal of useful → rich, renders…especially transparent → makes…transparent, and a chatty aside (we would gladly…turn the paper into a book) replaced by a sober statement of scope. Rendered from the paper’s own LaTeX; no wording invented for this poster.
Exhibit 6A long-mission brief. The contract for a five-hour unattended run: goals, fallback rules, and explicit stop conditions, written before the agent starts. The mission validates computed seismic sensitivity kernels against published reference results (Liu & Tromp 2008; Colombi 2012; Nissen-Meyer 2007). The human reads a report afterwards, not a chat.
Exhibit 7The personal-server interface. One config file per project tells the agents how to use the self-built compute server: where the remote mirror lives, which environment to activate, what to push, and what results to pull back. The comments record scars — one exclusion rule exists because of a specific incident, with its date.
Exhibit 8One node of a literature map — a different project, a different field. This reading note lives in a second, independent literature-mapping effort (the PLI paper's own review, separate from the thesis): machine-readable fields (model space, data space, prior type, citation edges) on top, prose assessment below, read from the actual source paper. Each objective-focused map runs its own version of this; the structure repeats because it works.
Exhibit 9The citation graph those notes generate. Rendered from the structured edges in the reading notes — not drawn by hand. This is what "the field's structure is mapped, not skimmed" looks like: reviewers of the map can trace every arrow back to a note, and every note back to the paper.
9
repositories under one plan-traceability protocol, enforced by git hooks
3
AI providers held to the same written contract; none is trusted more than the protocol
0
bytes of unpublished work ever transmitted; blocked mechanically, exceptions logged
5+ h
single unattended compute missions: solver builds, sensitivity kernels, remote ssh runs
"The point was never to think less.
It was to verify more, log everything, and waste nothing: to give one researcher the checking, auditing, and computing capacity of a small lab, without surrendering a single authorial decision."
Never draftsThe AI does not write final scientific prose. Editing is minimal-edit only, preserving the author's claims, voice, and citation intent.
Never inventsNo fabricated references, quotations, results, or novelty claims. Bibliography entries are verified against DOI registries before they are trusted.
Never unloggedPlans, commits, mission reports, verification verdicts, and every outbound query form a paper trail a skeptical examiner could walk end to end.
